chunks: Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام was brought a man who had been struck, and part of his speech had gone while part remained. So he apportioned his compensation according to the letters of the alphabet. Then he said, “Speak using the alphabet.” Whatever was missing from his speech was calculated accordingly. And the alphabet is twenty-eight letters, so he made it into twenty-eight parts; whatever was missing from his speech was calculated accordingly.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amir al-Mu'minin, Imam Ali عليه السلام, acting here as judicial authority
key_terms.تَكَلَّمْ: speak; an instruction to test the person’s remaining articulation
key_terms.جُزْءًا: a part or fraction; each letter counted as one proportional share
key_terms.حُرُوفِ ٱلْمُعْجَمِ: the letters of the alphabet used as the measure for assessing speech loss
key_terms.دِيَتَهُ: his diyah; the financial compensation due for bodily injury
key_terms.نَقَصَ: was deficient or missing; the portion of speech capability lost

ai.seo_question: How did Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام calculate diyah for a person who lost part of his speech?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling from Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام regarding compensation for partial loss of speech caused by injury. He assessed the diyah proportionally by measuring the injured person’s ability to articulate the twenty-eight letters of the alphabet, establishing a precise method for judicial evaluation.
